data.title: Skyworks Solutions drops 10%, halting recent upswing
data.description:
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS), a semiconductor company focused on analog and mixed-signal products, retreated just over 10% on Monday, pulling back sharply after a strong multi-session advance.

The stock closed the regular session at $79.26, down $9.09 from the prior close, with volume of 11.16 million shares running at roughly 1.8 times the one-month average. 

The stock had climbed 10 out of the previous 12 sessions.

data.title: Eli Lilly has more than 30% of new patients on oral weight-loss meds: exec
data.description:
• An Eli Lilly (LLY) executive said that the pharmaceutical giant has captured more than 30% of new U.S. patients on oral weight-loss drugs.
  • Lilly's oral obesity treatment, Foundayo (orforglipron), hit the market in early April, about three months after Novo Nordisk's (NVO) rival Wegovy (semaglutide) pill.
  • Speaking at the Morgan Stanley Global Healthcare Conference in New York, Lilly EVP Ilya Yuffa noted that the company's injectable weight-loss treatment, Zepbound (tirzepatide), is preferred among patients in the ​Medicare obesity drug pilot that began in July, Reuters reported. He added that 60%-70% of those in the program are new to GLP-1 therapies.
  • Yuffa's comments come after Novo Nordisk CEO Mike Doustdar in August said that the Wegovy pill had a 90% share of the oral obesity drugs market.

data.title: Toppoint Holdings announces reincorporation from Nevada to Delaware
data.description:
• Toppoint Holdings (TOPP) said on Monday it is expected to reincorporate from Nevada to Delaware on or about September 25, following shareholder approval on September 8.
  • The number of authorized common shares is expected to increase to 1B from 300M following the reincorporation, with no immediate change to shares outstanding.
  • Each outstanding common share will convert into one share of the Delaware, while existing options, warrants, and other equity securities will continue on the same terms.
  • No changes are expected to the company’s operations.

data.title: BAE Systems wins $818M U.S. Army armored vehicle contract boost
data.description:
• BAE Systems (BAESY)'s  Land & Armaments business secured an $818.4M U.S. Army contract modification for Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicles (AMPVs).
  • The modification lifts the contract’s total value to about $3.30B.
  • Moreover, the work will be carried out in York, Pennsylvania, with completion expected by May 31, 2030.
  • The Army has obligated the full $818.4M award using fiscal 2025 and 2026 procurement funds.
  • Army Contracting Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise slides 11% after Evercore ISI downgrade
data.description:
Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), an enterprise technology infrastructure company, tumbled almost 11% on Monday. The stock dropped $6.68 to close at $55.41 after Evercore ISI downgraded the stock to In-Line from Outperform, citing a more balanced risk/reward profile following a sharp run-up in the share price.

The decline came one session after HPE surged just over 12%, as the stock has seen choppy trading recently.

data.title: Intercont sets 25-for-1 reverse split to regain Nasdaq compliance
data.description:
• Intercont (Cayman) (NCT) announced on Monday that it will carry out a 25-for-1 reverse stock split effective September 17, 2026.
  • The move is aimed at restoring compliance with Nasdaq’s $1 minimum bid price requirement.
  • Starting September 17, the shares will trade on a split-adjusted basis under the same NCT ticker but with a new CUSIP.
  • Moreover, every 25 existing shares will become 1 share. The company’s issued Class A shares will fall from about 25.4M to 1.02M.
  • The shareholders do not need to take any action. Brokerage accounts will be adjusted automatically.
